evidence: Translucent pale blue-gray streak extending south-southeast from southern coast of Hawaii island, distinct from brighter white clouds; mask is 6896 km2, 154 km long, ocean-dominated so not a cloud-bank artifact. [E4, E6]

Wind from 71 deg (toward 251 deg) at 37.8 kmh vs measured plume drift toward 214 deg at 18.1 kmh with fit R2 0.98; difference ~37 deg agrees within ~45 deg, supporting south-southwest transport from the island. [E1, E5]

Geometric upwind end at 18.945N,-155.245E is 51.4 km from Kilauea summit vs 70.2 km from Mauna Loa; tracked 3-h source end at 19.06N,-155.445W is 42.1 km from Kilauea vs 49.2 km from Mauna Loa, trailing south from Kilauea side of island. [E5, E6]
USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW episodic_pause after Episode 55 ended 9:03am HST Oct 17, Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, favoring Kilauea as vog source. [E2]
FIRMS 2026-10-17 shows only Kilauea-summit thermal (316 volcanic_thermal pixels) and summit-proximal clusters within 2-4 km, no wildfire detections near plume upwind end to support smoke. [E3]
Mask land fraction 0.034 over Hawaii island only 0.022, no islands swallowed, indicating reliable over-water plume mask rather than land/cloud contamination. [E4]

evidence_cited.text: Translucent pale blue-gray streak extending south-southeast from southern coast of Hawaii island, distinct from brighter white clouds; mask is 6896 km2, 154 km long, ocean-dominated so not a cloud-bank artifact.

Wind from 71 deg (toward 251 deg) at 37.8 kmh vs measured plume drift toward 214 deg at 18.1 kmh with fit R2 0.98; difference ~37 deg agrees within ~45 deg, supporting south-southwest transport from the island.

Geometric upwind end at 18.945N,-155.245E is 51.4 km from Kilauea summit vs 70.2 km from Mauna Loa; tracked 3-h source end at 19.06N,-155.445W is 42.1 km from Kilauea vs 49.2 km from Mauna Loa, trailing south from Kilauea side of island.
USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW episodic_pause after Episode 55 ended 9:03am HST Oct 17, Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, favoring Kilauea as vog source.
FIRMS 2026-10-17 shows only Kilauea-summit thermal (316 volcanic_thermal pixels) and summit-proximal clusters within 2-4 km, no wildfire detections near plume upwind end to support smoke.
Mask land fraction 0.034 over Hawaii island only 0.022, no islands swallowed, indicating reliable over-water plume mask rather than land/cloud contamination.

classify.caveats: Kilauea was in episodic_pause with Episode 55 ending ~2h before image (19:03 UTC); residual degassing/vog is assumed but active fountaining had ceased. Wind-toward (251 deg) vs measured drift (214 deg) differs by ~37 deg, within tolerance but indicating some shear or age-related turning.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
